patient.name: Denis Okonkwo
patient.chief_complaint: Progressive distal leg weakness and sensory loss over 6 months, with new skin darkening, hair coarsening, and leg swelling
patient.hpi: Denis Okonkwo is a 47-year-old civil engineer presenting with a 6-month history of progressive bilateral leg weakness and sensory loss. His symptoms began with bilateral foot tingling and numbness, followed by progressive weakness over the subsequent 2 months, and he now has significant difficulty walking distances more than half a block without stopping. He notes that his symptoms began with what seemed like a typical neuropathy but he has developed several additional features that concern him: prominent bilateral ankle and calf swelling, a change in his skin color with darkening of his face and forearms, and coarsening of his body hair. He was diagnosed with prostate cancer in remission 6 years ago and is cancer-anxiety prone. He was initially evaluated by an oncologist who ordered imaging to exclude cancer recurrence — CT was negative. He saw a dermatologist for the skin changes who documented 'hyperpigmentation, uncertain etiology.' He also reports that his libido has significantly decreased over the past 6 months and he was found to have low testosterone on a routine check (188 ng/dL). He has had no fever, no night sweats, no lymph node swelling. He is a non-smoker and social drinker (2-3 drinks per week). His primary care physician has been perplexed by the combination of symptoms and referred him to neurology.
pmh: Prostate cancer (low-grade, localized — in remission 6 years, no active treatment)

report.summary: SEVERELY ABNORMAL NCS/EMG. DEMYELINATING SENSORIMOTOR POLYNEUROPATHY with superimposed axonal loss — mixed demyelinating and axonal pattern.

report.overall_impression: Severe demyelinating sensorimotor polyneuropathy with superimposed axonal loss. Markedly prolonged distal motor latencies, severely slowed conduction velocities, and reduced CMAP amplitudes across all tested motor nerves. Sural and median SNAP amplitudes severely reduced with slowed velocities. Needle EMG shows active and chronic denervation in distal musculature. Findings are consistent with a severe mixed demyelinating and axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy. Clinical correlation recommended.

specialized_test.impression: 1. Markedly prolonged distal motor latencies (peroneal 8.2 ms, tibial 8.8 ms, median 6.4 ms) with severely slowed conduction velocities (peroneal 31.4 m/s, tibial 32.8 m/s) and reduced CMAP amplitudes across all tested motor nerves. 2. Sural and median SNAP amplitudes severely reduced with slowed sensory velocities. 3. Needle EMG: active denervation (fibrillations) and chronic neuropathic motor units in distal upper and lower extremity musculature. Findings are consistent with a severe mixed demyelinating and axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy with symmetric four-limb involvement

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: POEMS syndrome (multifocal osteosclerotic myeloma, IgA lambda)

differential.key_features: Demyelinating polyneuropathy; differentiates from POEMS by absence of monoclonal protein, lambda restriction, elevated VEGF, and osteosclerotic lesions.
Demyelinating with terminal slowing; IgM (vs IgA/IgG lambda in POEMS); anti-MAG antibody.
Lytic (not sclerotic) bone lesions; renal failure, anemia, hypercalcemia.
Painful small-fiber + autonomic + cardiac amyloidosis; lambda light chain restriction.
No childhood features or family history.

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify reversible/treatable etiologies (diabetes, B12 deficiency, monoclonal gammopathy, thyroid disease)

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Length-dependent axonal vs demyelinating vs multifocal pattern; severity and distribution

optimal_actions.action: SPEP / IFE / serum free light chains; VEGF level; bone marrow biopsy; whole-body skeletal survey or FDG-PET/CT for osteosclerotic lesions; endocrine panel
optimal_actions.expected_finding: IgA lambda monoclonal protein, markedly elevated VEGF, multiple osteosclerotic lesions on skeletal survey supports POEMS

optimal_actions.action: FDG-PET/CT or whole-body MRI for osteosclerotic plasmacytoma

useless_tools.rationale: EEG is a cortical test and is non-contributory in peripheral nerve disease.
Head/brain CT has no role in peripheral neuropathy evaluation.
Brain MRI is not indicated in typical distal symmetric polyneuropathy without CNS signs.
Echocardiography is not indicated unless cardiac amyloid is suspected.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is not indicated unless there is syncope or symptomatic dysautonomia with arrhythmia concern.

sequence_constraints.reason: Tier the workup — basic labs first, then targeted electrodiagnostic and tissue studies.

critical_actions: Send SPEP / IFE / light chains AND VEGF — POEMS is defined by lambda monoclonal protein + elevated VEGF
Whole-body skeletal survey / FDG-PET/CT for osteosclerotic plasmacytoma (multifocal here)
Endocrine workup (TSH, testosterone, prolactin, cortisol, glucose) and skin / organomegaly exam
Refer to hematology for definitive treatment (radiation for limited lesions, ASCT or systemic therapy for multifocal disease)
contraindicated_actions: Do not label as 'CIDP' and miss POEMS — definitive treatment is markedly different
Do not give chronic IVIG in suspected POEMS — typically refractory
key_reasoning_points: Demyelinating polyneuropathy + IgA lambda monoclonal + osteosclerotic lesions = POEMS
VEGF is the most sensitive biomarker
Disseminated osteosclerotic disease requires systemic therapy (ASCT)
